proposal.diagnosis: The issue lies in how the tokenizer handles input starting with a semicolon `;`. The code incorrectly processes characters following `;` as part of the token stream instead of treating them as a comment that should be ignored. Specifically, at line 165, when `ch` is not `59` (semicolon), it sets `id=2`, indicating a comment start. However, subsequent processing fails to correctly handle cases where characters after `;` are not part of the comment structure, leading to erroneous token generation.

` produces an error token for `6#l`, indicating improper handling of the semicolon and subsequent characters.
Line 165 sets `id=2` when `ch != 59`, which incorrectly flags non-comment content as a comment start, leading to misclassification of tokens.

The exact implementation may vary slightly, but the core issue remains the same.
proposal.assumption: The comment processing logic fails to reset state after encountering `;`, leading to subsequent token misclassification.

edits.rationale: Ensure that only characters following `;` until newline are treated as part of the comment.
edits.replacement: if(ch == 59) { id = 2; ch = get_char(tp); while(ch != '\n' && ch != EOF) { ch = get_char(tp); } } else if(ch == '"') id = 1;

proposal.expected_effect: Properly skip all characters after `;` until newline or EOF, preventing any tokens from being generated for the comment content.
